floor_history.headline: Recon: baseline floor 8, gap is prologue callee-save ORDER (not RA); killed H-s1 count-first reorder (8→13); frontier H-s2/s3/s4 on axes that shift first-write sequence without cheat-siblings' pin+dum
H-s5 CONFIRMED: `saved; count=3; idx; base; elem;` drops floor 8->4 by making count's pseudo win s0 (matches target); H-s3/H-s4 KILLED

frontier.hypothesis: H-s6: force a1's first-use in RTL to precede a0's, e.g. by a legitimate early expression that references a1 without dead-code semantics
frontier.mechanism: sched1 orders arg-copy insns by first-use position. If a1 is textually first-used before a0, `move s1, a1` may schedule ahead of `move s4, a0`, matching target's sw interleave.
frontier.next_probe: Identify any legitimate structural reordering that references a1 (or a2) in the block before the `idx = a0 & 0xFF` compute WITHOUT a dead store / self-assign / conditional-dead-store (all forbidden). Consider whether the compare `if (idx != 1)` inside the loop can be replaced by a `switch (a0 & 0xFF)`-shaped dispatch that binds idx via a2-parameterised expression (weak — likely still uses a0 first).

frontier.hypothesis: H-s7: type-narrow one arg to alter parameter-pseudo priority
frontier.mechanism: Parameter types (u16 vs s32) may change GCC 2.7.2 pseudo-numbering or size-priority for global.c's allocno_compare, altering which arg wins first hard-reg pick.
frontier.next_probe: Grep call sites of tslPolyF4Init (only src/system.c:1208 `tslPolyF4Init(9, 0, 0)` known) to determine if any arg has a natural narrower type; if so, try `s32 tslPolyF4Init(u8 a0, ...)` etc. Since tslPolyF4Init(9,0,0) fits any narrowing, this is safe to probe without touching call sites.

frontier.hypothesis: H-s8: interleave-rule park (owner-gated escalation), citing sibling-evidence that ONLY a regfix `reorder` closes this plateau
frontier.mechanism: func_80080258/func_80080390 use `reorder 3,18,4,17,5,6,7,19,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16 @ 3-19` alongside their cheat pins to fix the SAME arg-copy interleave. That regfix would be forbidden here, but its existence is evidence the fork's sched1+assign_parms interleave cannot be steered by any C source producing our allocation shape.
frontier.next_probe: Reserved for a later session AFTER H-s6/H-s7 are measured dead. Do NOT owner-gate now — this session has open axes.
